scenarios.name: fan_running_during_occupied_hours
scenarios.description: The normal case: the exhaust fan runs inside the occupied schedule.

scenarios.name: fan_off_during_unoccupied_hours
scenarios.description: The fan conjunct blocking on its own: unoccupied and the fan is off, which is the outcome the rule exists to produce.

scenarios.name: fan_running_unoccupied_with_no_override
scenarios.description: The reference condition. Fan proven on, outside the schedule, nothing holding it; TrueDelay asserts at exactly alarm_delay (900 s).

scenarios.name: demand_override_justifies_the_run
scenarios.description: The override conjunct blocking on its own: same after-hours run, but a demand override (kitchen hood, restroom call, lab purge) is holding the fan on legitimately.

scenarios.name: fan_stops_on_the_alarm_tick
scenarios.description: The delay edge from below: the fan stops at exactly 900 s, so the condition is false on the tick the delay would have matured and nothing is reported.

scenarios.name: fan_stops_one_tick_later
scenarios.description: The same edge from above: one tick of alarm at 900 s, then clear.

scenarios.name: override_drops_and_starts_the_clock
scenarios.description: A legitimate override expires at 1200 s and the fan keeps running anyway. The 1200 s already elapsed does not count — the alarm lands 900 s after the justification disappears.

scenarios.name: schedule_resumes_and_clears_the_alarm
scenarios.description: Recovery: the alarm asserts at 900 s and the occupied schedule opens at 1800 s, dropping it on that tick — TrueDelay delays the rising edge only.
